answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a ivory as the anchor of the cost.
